Hardware-accelerated Multimodality Volume Fusion is a technique for combining multiple volume datasets (e.g., MR and PET) into a single image representation using graphics hardware to solve depth cueing problems and reduce processing time compared to software-based methods [S1].

The claim states that Hardware-accelerated Multimodality Volume Fusion combines multiple volume datasets (e.g., MR and PET) into a single image representation using graphics hardware to solve depth cueing problems and reduce processing time compared to software-based methods. Source [S1] explicitly confirms all these points: it proposes a technique using graphics hardware to combine volumes (MR and PET are mentioned in the abstract and experimental results), solves the depth cueing problem, and achieves a 5 to 6 times speed enhancement (625 msec vs 3703 msec) compared to software-based methods.
